newsitem.title: USA: Lyondell, Millennium in $5 billion chemical venture.
newsitem.headline: Lyondell, Millennium in $5 billion chemical venture.

text.p: Lyondell Petrochemical Co. and Millennium Chemicals Inc. said Monday they have formed a joint venture of their bulk chemicals operations in a deal valued at $5 billion.

The venture, designed to cut costs in the up-and-down petrochemicals industry, will create the largest producer of ethylene and polyethylene in North America. Ethylenes are petrochemicals used in the manufacture of plastic.

Lyondell, based in Houston, will own 57 percent of the new company, and New Jersey-based Millennium the remaining 43 percent. The new company will control around 4 percent of the global ethylene market and 6 percent of the global polyethylene market.
The companies expect the partnership to generate more than $150 million in annual pretax profits on annual revenues of $5 billion.
The venture will be governed by a six-member committee co-chaired by Lyondell President Dan Smith and Millennium Chairman William Landuyt.
Smith also will serve as chief executive of the company, which will be headquartered in Houston.
Lyondell's Smith said the venture would enable both companies to survive a downturn in an industry that is facing higher production capacity and the likelihood of lower prices next year.
"This venture will make us stronger going into the next trough," Smith said.
Smith also said the joint venture would free up resources for Lyondell to expand more profitable businesses, or possibly to buy back stock.
The companies said the combination, which will have $1.745 billion in debt, will have book assets of about $5 billion.

The companies said they expect a one-time savings gain of $100 million as a result of the venture, with $150 million in savings annually by the end of 1999. The deal is expected to close by the end of this year.
They said the new company will consist of 13 facilities on the Gulf Coast and in the Midwest, producing ethylene, propylene, polyethylene, polypropylene, ethyl alcohol and related chemical products.
Separately, Lyondell said Monday its second-quarter earnings rose sharply, bolstered by higher petrochemical product prices and lower crude oil prices.

Lyondell's net income climbed to $93 million, or $1.17 a share, compared with $15 million, or 19 cents a share in the same year-ago period. Sales totalled $789 million in the second quarter, up from $613 million in the year-ago period.
Lyondell's stock rose 44 cents to $26.19 in late consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Millennium rose 87.5 cents to $21.69 a share, also on the NYSE.
